page: Amazon Web Services x8i.32xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs operating at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz. Cache architecture consists of 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a massive 480 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets, providing hardware acceleration for vectorized operations and quantized matrix math.

The defining characteristic of the x8i.32xlarge is its memory density, providing 2048 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 7 GHz. This translates to an expansive ratio of 16 GB of memory per core. The instance delivers a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence and operating file systems must rely on external network-attached block storage volumes. In addition, no physical GPUs are attached to this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations place the server in the top tier for multi-core compute capability, achieving a multi-core stress-ng score of 138370.32 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 22488. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 10225.05 GB/sec, while uncached large-block sequential reads hit 344.9 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, the system recorded 211.23 million Redis SET operations per second and demonstrated top-tier prompt processing in large language model inference tests. However, single-core CPU throughput registers in average tiers compared to compute-specialized alternatives, reflecting an architecture focused on parallel throughput and extreme RAM density rather than maximum single-thread frequency.

Given its balance of 128 vCPUs and two terabytes of system memory, the x8i.32xlarge offers qualitative efficiency when running memory-bound enterprise systems that would otherwise require multiple smaller instances. Tradeoffs include reliance on networked storage for disk I/O and moderate single-threaded execution speeds. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis or Memcached distributed caching layers, large-scale graph analysis, and in-memory big data processing frameworks.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and designed for high-density in-memory computing. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors, it provides 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs running at up to 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache and advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance features 2048 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 7 GHz, delivering an expansive 16 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation alongside 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent filesystems. Benchmark testing shows top-tier multi-threaded processing, robust uncached memory throughput, and exceptional Redis throughput reaching over 211 million operations per second. The instance provides strong hardware density for organizations consolidating massive memory footprints, making it well matched for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching clusters, and high-capacity data processing pipelines.
